column3: “in the days to come” renders “in the end of the days.”
“Uncontrolled” renders a rare word that may mean “reckless” or “boiling over.”
“implements” renders an uncertain word, which some take as “swords” or “plans.”
“my glory” may be vocalized as “my liver,” that is, “my being,” and “lamed oxen” renders “hamstrung an ox.”
“shall praise you” plays on the name “Judah.”
“Until Shiloh comes” is a disputed phrase that may also mean “until he comes to whom it belongs” or “until tribute comes to him.”
“dull from wine” renders “darker than wine,” and “white from milk” may be “whiter than milk.”
“a strong donkey” renders “a donkey of bone,” and “the sheepfolds” renders a word of uncertain meaning (perhaps “saddlebags”).
“A horned snake” renders “shephiphon,” a rare word for a kind of viper.
“raiders shall raid him” and “he shall raid” play on the name “Gad.”
“He gives beautiful words” may also be read “who bears lovely fawns.”
“a fruitful bough” renders “a son of a fruitful one,” which may also mean “a wild colt,” and “Its branches” renders “daughters.”
“the Mighty One of Jacob” renders “the Abir of Jacob,” and the parenthesis renders an obscure line.
“my ancestors” follows the Hebrew vowels (“those who conceived me”); the Greek reads “the eternal mountains,” and “the one distinguished” renders “nazir.”
